newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB completes Brazilian deal.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB completes Brazilian deal.

text.p: Lloyds TSB Group Plc said it unit Lloyds Bank has completed a deal to buy the consumer finance business and some other assets of Brazil's Banco Multiplic SA (BMSA), its 50 percent-owned associate.
As part of the deal, Lloyds will relinquish its investment in BMSA to the other principal shareholder Multiplic Empreendimentos e Comercio SA.
Lloyds said the acquisition premium was $218 million which will be satisfied by Lloyds giving up its investment in BMSA which had a book value of 106 million stg.
The consumer finance business, which trades as Losango, was formed in 1971 and is the leading business of its type in Brazil, financing mainly white and soft goods.
BMSA, made a profit of $146 million in 1996.

"Brazil has an increasingly important consumer market," said Lloyds TSB international banking director David Pirrie in a statement. "Through this deal, we will acquire 100 percent control over the leading provider of consumer finance in that market.

News of the deal first broke in February and Lloyds has since said it has no other specific deals in mind in Latin America despite the fact that it is encouraged by the improving economic conditions in much of the continent.
Lloyds has been present in Brazil since 1862 and currently has 11 branches covering commercial, private and investment banking.
The bank was heavily involved in lending to sovereign countries in Latin America and consequently suffered during the 1980s debt crisis.
